forecast-period.text: A low pressure system and associated trough continue moving over southern SA tonight and will move into the eastern states by late Tuesday. A high pressure system will move in from the west to be over SA on Wednesday. Another trough approaches the southwest during Thursday evening, and may linger about the western parts of SA before another high moves across the south over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers about the Agricultural Area, the Flinders Ranges and adjacent areas, tending to rain about central and eastern parts of the Agricultural Area during the morning, before contracting eastwards during the day. Possible thunderstorms about the northeast during the early morning. Maximum temperatures generally below average. Southwesterly winds, fresh about central and eastern coastal fringes and about eastern inland areas, easing during the evening. Winds shifting east to southeasterly in the west throughout the day.

Showers, tending to rain, with local heavy falls possible, clearing from the northwest. Thunderstorms about the Northern Agricultural Area and Pastoral districts, possibly severe mainly about the central north, easing into the evening. North to northeasterly winds, ahead of a fresh west to southwesterly change extending from the west.

Possible early morning fog and frost about the Eyre Peninsula and adjacent areas, as well as on and east of the Flinders Ranges. Slight chance of an isolated morning shower about the Southern Agricultural Area. Maximum temperatures generally below average, tending to near average in the southwest. Southwest to southeasterly winds in the east, easing to light and variable in the southeast during the evening. Winds tending northeast to northerly in the west.

Possible early morning frost on and east of the Flinders Ranges and morning fog about the southeast. Mostly dry, until showers and possible thunderstorms develop about the far west from the late afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures above average, tending below average in the northeast. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending easterly in the northeast.

text.p: Possible patchy early morning frost about the Flinders Ranges. Showers and possible thunderstorms about western parts, mostly dry elsewhere. Maximum temperatures near to below average, tending above average in the southeast. Northeast to northwesterly winds, ahead of a weak west to southwesterly change in the far west during the day. Winds tending southeasterly throughout from the evening.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: Broadly 1 to 5 mm, increasing to 5 to 15 mm about parts of the Pastoral districts and a further 15 to 30 mm about parts of the West Coast and Agricultural Areas. Falls of 20 to 40 mm possible about southern parts of Eyre, Yorke and Fleurieu Peninsulas and the Mount Lofty Ranges, with isolated localised falls of 40 to 60 mm in these areas and with thunderstorms.
